collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 35 or older and a young adult, 18-25)

collection.description: A young villager asks an older one what they want from life and is told this, mostly: explain, or ask what they want.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend), who is young and full of plans, has asked (subject) what (subject.he/she) wants out of life. (subject) has a hut, good friends, work (subject.he/she) doesn't mind, a favorite spot on the beach, and a mango tree that's almost ready. (subject.He/she) thinks about it, then says, "This, mostly." (friend) is baffled. "But don't you want MORE?"

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) thinks about how to say it. "I used to want more. Then one day I noticed I already liked what I had. So I stopped chasing and started enjoying." (friend) looks doubtful. "That sounds boring." (subject) laughs. "It might be, for you. You go and want more. It's a good thing to want. Just look up now and then and see if you've already got it."

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) asks what (friend) wants. (friend) talks for a long time: a canoe, a big hut, to be the best fisher on Isola, to travel, to be famous for something. (subject) listens to all of it. "Good," (subject.he/she) says at the end. "Go and get some of it." (friend) is a little surprised (subject) isn't trying to talk (friend.him/her) out of it. (subject) was young too, once.
